name: Red-bellied Macaw
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to the guianas, trinidad, northern bolivia, and amazonian brazil
description: Small green macaw of lowland rainforest. Favors swampy areas, especially those with palm trees, which it uses for nesting.

name: Chinese Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Eastern siberia to southeastern tibet and southern china; winters to northern indochina
description: Typical brown bush-warbler; forages quietly deep in dense undergrowth. Prefers wet areas such as reedbeds, riparian shrubbery, and marshy groves.

name: Chilean Skua
rangeDescription: Coasts of southern chile and southern argentina; ranges north to tropics
description: Rather large, dark, stocky gull-like seabird with big white wing patches (seen in flight). In summer often seen flying over Patagonian steppe or associating with Kelp Gulls at beaches, dumps, river mouths, and lakes near the coast.

name: Yellow-faced Parrot
rangeDescription: Interior brazil (maranhão) to northern paraguay and eastern bolivia
description: A very distinctive mostly green parrot with a yellow face, a yellowish belly, and orange-red thighs. Note the dark upper bill.

name: Yellow-throated Antwren
rangeDescription: Far eastern colombia, southwestern venezuela, and northwestern amazonian brazil
description: Tiny antwren, heavily streaked with black and white above, solid yellow below. Females have a tawny-colored head.

name: Madagascar Blue-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Humid forest of eastern madagascar
description: Medium-sized chunky pigeon that is dark blue with a maroon tail. Appears short-tailed in flight.

name: Rockwarbler
rangeDescription: Sandstone outcrops between hunter river and bega, coastal new south wales
description: Small terrestrial bird of Hawkesbury Sandstone region of southern New South Wales. Brown above, reddish brown below, with paler throat.

name: White-crowned Parrot
rangeDescription: Caribbean slope of southeastern mexico to western panama
description: Medium-size, blue-green parrot of tropical lowlands, mainly in humid forest and forest edge. The big white crown patch and white throat on a bluish head are distinctive; also note the pinkish-red patch under the tail.

name: Yellow-billed Spoonbill
rangeDescription: Australia; vagrant to tasmania and new zealand
description: Large dull-white bird with a long, spoon-shaped bill. Plumage often appears dirty.

name: Abyssinian Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Savanna and juniper highlands of ethiopia and eritrea
description: A small, short-tailed woodpecker of the Abyssinian highlands. Note the pure golden-green back and the white facial streaks that frame a dark cheek.

name: Uniform Finch
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil and northeastern argentina
description: Slender finch found at forest borders where it is especially associated with bamboo. Usually forages on or near the ground.

name: Hawaiian Hawk
rangeDescription: Forest of hawaii (hawaiian islands)
description: A medium-sized, compact hawk with broad wings. It is the only resident hawk in Hawaii and occurs only on Hawaii Island.

name: Sierra Nevada Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Shy and skulking brushfinch restricted to cloud forest in Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. Quite distinctive in its limited range, with a black face and breast spot, white throat, and striped head.

name: Serra do Mar Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Coastal mountains of southeastern brazil (espírito santo to northern rio grande do sul)
description: Tiny flycatcher with a long slender tail. Differs from other tyrannulets in being mostly bright olive-green above and gray below with darkish ear patches, prominent white eyerings, and pinkish (not dark) legs.

name: Yellow-thighed Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of costa rica and western panama
description: Unique sooty-gray bird with odd yellow tufts of feathers at the base of each leg. Darker black on head and wings.

name: Jamaican Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Jamaica
description: A striking medium-sized species of wooded habitats. The white face framed by the red of its nape and crown and its finely barred black-and-white back is distinctive; resembles no other species in its range.

name: Creamy-bellied Antwren
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of peru (huánuco to cusco)
description: Small antwren found in the canopy of foothill forests of the eastern Andes in central Peru. Note the black cap, striped face, white wingbars, and lack of rufous in the wing.

name: Dimorphic Dwarf-Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Central and southern philippines
description: A small kingfisher of lowland and foothill forest. Deep blue above with bright orange underparts, an orange spot between the bill and eye, a white throat and patch behind the cheek, and a bright red bill and legs.

name: Short-billed Pipit
rangeDescription: Far southeastern brazil to paraguay, uruguay, and northern argentina
description: Slender brown and buff bird with a streaked breast found in short grassland, pastures, and sparsely vegetated plains. White outer tail feathers are most evident in flight.

name: Gorgeted Wood-Quail
rangeDescription: Temperate eastern andes of colombia (santander and cundinamarca)
description: Scarce quail restricted to cloud forest in the northern half of Colombia’s eastern Andes. Adult has distinctive black and white crescents on the throat, which may be reduced or lacking in young birds.
